thread:
maya: Heads-up — saw a regression in prod canary for the flash-fused attention path, ~20% p99 increase on responses that hit KV-cache writes. nsys trace attached to the bug report: https://internal.perf/redwood/trace/1812345678 :grimacing:

sam: which workload / batch distribution?

maya: small batches (effective batch 4-8), mixed seq lengths (32/128). Kernel selector ended up choosing flash_fused_attn_v2 for many of the 32-token requests even though the exec time per token was worse. Timeline shows repeated preemption on KV write path around the same time as the fused kernel launches.

liam: do you have the nsys timeline snippet? can you paste the hotspot timeline?

maya: pasted below — trimmed for thread:
```
nsys timeline snippet (top lanes):
[GPU activity] 14:03:12.130 - flash_fused_attn_v2  (Duration: 1.8ms)
[GPU activity] 14:03:12.132 - kv_cache_write_kernel    (Duration: 0.9ms)
[GPU activity] 14:03:12.133 - flash_fused_attn_v2  (Duration: 2.0ms)
[GPU activity] 14:03:12.135 - kv_cache_write_kernel    (Duration: 1.1ms)
[CPU activity] 14:03:12.129 - service thread enqueues batch
[CPU activity] 14:03:12.131 - kernel_selector: chose flash_fused_attn_v2 (heuristic: seq<=64 && batch<=16)
```
The kv_cache_write kernel has a lot of SM serialization in this trace — nvprof counters show high memory pipe utilization and long back-to-back WAR stalls.

anita: perf-bot posted aggregated counters earlier: 
perf-bot: {"trace_id":"1812345678","kernel":"kv_cache_write_kernel","sm_efficiency":"62%","dram_throughput":"420 GB/s","l2_miss_rate":"7%","active_war_stalls":"high"}

sam: interesting — do we see write amplification on the KV side? i.e. multiple writes per token due to partial flush?

maya: yeah that's a clue. The runtime tries to compact KV writes into aligned chunks, but the fused-attn variant interleaves compute and kv writes more aggressively, which causes small-sized concurrent writes from multiple warps. That pattern kills coalescing and increases memory stalls.

liam: Could kernel selection be preferring fused-attn because of a stale perf profile? Maybe earlier on larger batches it was best, but with current batch distribution small-batch latency matters.

maya: exactly. The selection heuristic is very simple: if seq_len <= 64 choose fused, else fallback. It doesn't account for concurrent KV write contention or observed memory pipe pressure.

sam: reproduce locally? which machine / GPU?

maya: repro on g5x2-lon-12 (A10G) and gtx-like in perf lab. I have an nsys of a smaller run here: https://internal.perf/redwood/nsys/1812345678-run1.nsys

anita: steps I propose:
- rerun nsys with CUPTI counters for memory (l2, dram, pipe_util) for both fused and non-fused variants
- add a short microbench that isolates KV write kernel (single-threaded writes with same stride) to measure coalescing impact
- instrument kernel_selector to emit a lightweight counter when it picks fused for seq<=64 so we can correlate selection rates with regression windows

liam: also log batch-size histogram at enqueue time and include the scatter of seq lengths in that batch. Our heuristics should be distribution-aware, not just per-request seq_len.

maya: did a quick micro-run: when forcing unfused_attn we see kv_cache_write kernel is 30-40% shorter and SM utilization climbs to 78%. With fused the write kernel is longer and causes subsequent fused kernel launches to stall waiting on memory. So fused is winning compute but losing memory.

sam: sounds like an inter-kernel interference problem. Could we try staging KV writes on the CPU-side (coalescing) and then push a bigger aligned write to GPU? Risk: adds latency for single-shot small requests. Might be worth experiment as opt-in flag.

maya: agreed. Another idea: change kernel selection to fall back to non-fused when concurrent KV-write-rate > threshold. We can add a runtime metric: "kv_writes_per_ms" and feed it into selector. Lightweight and incremental.

anita: to prioritize — we should get a reproducible perf test and a perf dashboard tile showing fused vs unfused p99 over last 24h. If we can correlate with deploy windows we can roll back policy if needed.

liam: I can add the dashboard tile. Also, suggest running a perfetto capture to get full system context (CPU scheduling, memcpy, PCIe stalls). nsys sometimes hides CPU-side host waits.

maya: good call. I already started a perfetto on a repro run — link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/1812345678. That showed long host->device memcpy bursts lining up with KV writes. Looks like the host thread batches up small copies then pushes them, creating small bursts.

sam: then host-side coalescing seems promising. For a quick mitigation we can throttle the number of concurrent KV write submissions per device queue. If we limit to 2 concurrent writers we might recover coalescing and reduce stalls. Can we toggle that via env var?

maya: yes kernel-queue depth is a runtime param. I'll flip it on a canary and run a smoke.

perf-bot: Automation note: regression alert created (REG-54321) for p99 increase >15% on canary cluster. Attaching GPU traces.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy rolling back to previous selector config in cluster canary-3 now.

anita: follow-ups for next week:
- maya: microbench for kv coalescing (due EOD Wed)
- sam: selector telemetry flag + env var throttle (due Thu)
- liam: dashboard tile + perfetto vs nsys comparison doc (due Fri)
- ops: run canary with throttle and telemetry enabled, capture traces

maya: thanks — I'll post the microbench results and attach the trimmed nsys/perfetto snippets. Please ping me if you need the raw traces. :thumbsup:

sam: nice work catching this. If the throttle helps we can make it dynamic in Optimize (recommendation engine) later.

liam: note for future: when adding fused kernels that touch KV cache we should include a small mem-access model for selector to estimate interference costs. saves headaches.

maya: agreed. closing loop once canary runs complete.
